cognition_match.developer_quote: REST v2 and gRPC divergent validation: REST v2 accepting values the gRPC path rejects (maintainers treat cross-channel inconsistency as a defect and fix it)
cognition_match.note: This case is inverse: contract documents top-level parameter, implementation only validates in params. Similar category of API surface inconsistency but different manifestation.

verdicts.rationale: NOT a missing validation bug. Validation IS present and working correctly in source code (handler_v2.go:2008-2023). The issue is a contract-implementation mismatch: structured_contract.json lists consistencyLevel as a top-level parameter, but the actual implementation only reads it from httpReq.Params['consistencyLevel']. Invalid values ARE rejected when passed in the correct location (params). Top-level consistencyLevel field is silently ignored (not a CollectionReq struct field), which is poor UX but not the 'missing validation' defect claimed. The bug report misidentified a parameter location design decision as a missing validation issue.
